title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Water Pollution

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purpose of protecting and improving the environment, preventing and controlling water pollution, protecting water ecology, ensuring the safety of drinking water, maintaining public health, advancing the construction of ecological civilization, and promoting the sustainable development of the economy and society.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to the prevention and control of pollution of surface water bodies such as rivers, lakes, canals, ditches, and reservoirs, as well as groundwater bodies, within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
The prevention and control of marine pollution shall be governed by the Marine Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 The prevention and control of water pollution shall adhere to the principles of giving priority to prevention, combining prevention with control, and comprehensive treatment, giving priority to the protection of drinking water sources, strictly controlling industrial pollution and urban domestic pollution, preventing and controlling agricultural non-point source pollution, actively promoting the construction of ecological treatment projects, and preventing, controlling, and reducing water environmental pollution and ecological damage.

Article 4 People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate water environmental protection work into national economic and social development plans.
Local people's governments at all levels shall be responsible for the water environment quality within their respective administrative regions and shall take timely measures to prevent and control water pollution.

Article 5 Provinces, cities, counties, and townships shall establish a river chief system to organize and lead, at different levels and sections, the protection of water resources, management of water area shorelines, prevention and control of water pollution, and water environment treatment of rivers and lakes within their respective administrative regions.

Article 6 The State shall implement a target responsibility system and an assessment and evaluation system for water environmental protection, and shall take the completion of water environmental protection targets as part of the assessment and evaluation of local people's governments and their leading officials.

Article 7 The State shall encourage and support scientific and technological research on water pollution prevention and control, and the promotion and application of advanced and applicable technologies, and shall strengthen the publicity and education on water environmental protection.

Article 8 The State shall establish and improve an ecological protection compensation mechanism for water environment in areas located in drinking water source protection zones and upstream areas of rivers, lakes, and reservoirs through financial transfer payments and other means.

Article 9 The competent department of environmental protection under the people's government at or above the county level shall exercise unified supervision and management over the prevention and control of water pollution.
The maritime administration authority of the competent department of transportation shall exercise supervision and management over the prevention and control of pollution of water areas by ships.
The departments of water administration, land and resources, health, construction, agriculture, fisheries, and other relevant departments under the people's government at or above the county level, as well as the basin water resources protection agencies for important rivers and lakes, shall, within their respective functions and duties, exercise supervision and management over relevant water pollution prevention and control.

Article 10 The discharge of water pollutants shall not exceed the water pollutant discharge standards and the total discharge amount control indexes for key water pollutants prescribed by the State or local authorities.

Article 11 Any unit or individual shall have the obligation to protect the water environment and the right to report any act that pollutes or damages the water environment.
People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant competent departments shall commend and reward units and individuals that have made remarkable achievements in the work of water pollution prevention and control.

Article 12 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall formulate national water environment quality standards.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate local standards for items not specified in the national water environment quality standards, and shall report them to the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council for recordation.

Article 13 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council, together with the competent department of water administration under the State Council and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, may, based on the use functions of the water bodies of important river and lake basins determined by the State and the economic and technological conditions of the relevant areas, determine the water environment quality standards applicable to the provincial boundary water bodies of such important river and lake basins, which shall come into force after being submitted to and approved by the State Council.

Article 14 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall, in accordance with the national water environment quality standards and the national economic and technological conditions, formulate national water pollutant discharge standards.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may formulate local water pollutant discharge standards for items not specified in the national water pollutant discharge standards; and for items already specified in the national water pollutant discharge standards, they may formulate local water pollutant discharge standards that are stricter than the national ones. Local water pollutant discharge standards must be reported to the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council for recordation.
Where pollutants are discharged into water bodies for which local water pollutant discharge standards already exist, those local water pollutant discharge standards shall be followed.

Article 15 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in a timely manner, revise the water environment quality standards and water pollutant discharge standards in accordance with the requirements of water pollution prevention and control and the national or local economic and technological conditions.

Article 16 The prevention and control of water pollution shall be planned in a unified manner by river basin or by region. The basin water pollution prevention and control plans for important rivers and lakes determined by the State shall be formulated by the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council together with the departments of comprehensive economic macro-control and water administration under the State Council and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and shall be submitted to the State Council for approval.
For other inter-provincial (autonomous region, municipality directly under the Central Government) rivers and lakes not covered by the preceding paragraph, the basin water pollution prevention and control plans shall be formulated by the competent departments of environmental protection of the relevant provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government together with the water administration departments and other relevant departments at the same level and the relevant people's governments of cities and counties, based on the basin water pollution prevention and control plans for important rivers and lakes determined by the State and the local actual conditions, and after being reviewed by the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, shall be submitted to the State Council for approval.
For inter-county rivers and lakes within a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, the basin water pollution prevention and control plans shall be formulated by the competent department of environmental protection of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government together with the water administration department and other relevant departments at the same level, based on the basin water pollution prevention and control plans for important rivers and lakes determined by the State and the local actual conditions, and shall be submitted to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval and reported to the State Council for recordation.
The approved water pollution prevention and control plans shall be the basic basis for preventing and controlling water pollution, and any revision of the plans must be approved by the original approving authority.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the basin water pollution prevention and control plans for rivers and lakes approved according to law, organize the formulation of water pollution prevention and control plans for their respective administrative regions.

Article 17 Relevant city and county people's governments shall, in accordance with the requirements of the water environment quality improvement targets determined in the water pollution prevention and control plans, formulate plans for achieving the standards within a prescribed time limit and take measures to meet the standards on schedule.
Relevant city and county people's governments shall report such plans for achieving the standards within a prescribed time limit to the people's government at the next higher level for recordation and make them public.

Article 18 When reporting the environmental conditions and the completion of environmental protection targets to the people's congress at the same level or its standing committee each year, the city and county people's governments shall report the implementation of the plans for achieving water environment quality standards within a prescribed time limit and make such information public.

Article 19 For construction projects and other water facilities that directly or indirectly discharge pollutants into water bodies, whether newly built, reconstructed, or expanded, an environmental impact assessment shall be conducted according to law.
Where a construction unit builds, reconstructs, or expands a sewage outlet in a river or lake, it shall obtain the consent of the competent department of water administration or the basin management agency; where navigation or fishery waters are involved, the competent department of environmental protection, when reviewing and approving the environmental impact assessment document, shall solicit the opinions of the competent departments of transportation and fisheries.
The water pollution prevention and control facilities of a construction project shall be designed, constructed, and put into use simultaneously with the main project. The water pollution prevention and control facilities shall meet the requirements of the approved or recorded environmental impact assessment document.

Article 20 The State shall implement a total discharge amount control system for key water pollutants.
The total discharge amount control indexes for key water pollutants shall, after the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council solicits opinions from the relevant departments under the State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, be submitted to the State Council by the competent department together with the department of comprehensive economic macro-control under the State Council for approval and then issued for implementation.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall reduce and control the total discharge amount of key water pollutants within their respective administrative regions in accordance with the provisions of the State Council. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council together with the relevant departments under the State Council.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, based on the water environment quality conditions within their respective administrative regions and the needs of water pollution prevention and control work, implement total discharge amount control for water pollutants other than the national key water pollutants.
For a region where the total discharge amount control indexes for key water pollutants are exceeded or the water environment quality improvement targets are not fulfilled, the competent department of environmental protection under the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, together with the relevant departments, hold talks with the principal leading official of the people's government of that region, and shall suspend the approval of environmental impact assessment documents for construction projects that would increase the total discharge amount of key water pollutants. The circumstances of such talks shall be made public.

Article 21 Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators that directly or indirectly discharge industrial wastewater, medical sewage, and other wastewater and sewage that shall be discharged only after obtaining a pollutant discharge permit according to relevant provisions shall obtain a pollutant discharge permit; the operating units of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities shall also obtain a pollutant discharge permit. The pollutant discharge permit shall specify the types, concentrations, total amounts, discharge destinations, and other requirements for discharging water pollutants. The specific measures for pollutant discharge permits shall be prescribed by the State Council.
Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators are prohibited from discharging into water bodies the wastewater or sewage specified in the preceding paragraph without a pollutant discharge permit or in violation of the provisions of the pollutant discharge permit.

Article 22 Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators that discharge pollutants into water bodies shall set up sewage outlets in accordance with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council; where sewage outlets are set up in rivers or lakes, the provisions of the competent department of water administration under the State Council shall also be complied with.

Article 23 Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and monitoring standards, conduct self-monitoring of the water pollutants they discharge and retain original monitoring records. Key pollutant discharging units shall also install automatic monitoring equipment for water pollutant discharge, connect it with the monitoring equipment of the competent department of environmental protection, and ensure the normal operation of the monitoring equipment. The specific measures shall be prescribed by the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council.
The list of key pollutant discharging units that shall install automatic monitoring equipment for water pollutant discharge shall be determined by the competent department of environmental protection under the local people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts, in consultation with the relevant departments at the same level, based on the environmental capacity of the administrative region, the requirements of the total discharge amount control indexes for key water pollutants, and the types, quantities, and concentrations of water pollutants discharged by the pollutant discharging units.

Article 24 Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators subject to pollutant discharge permit management shall be responsible for the authenticity and accuracy of monitoring data.
If the competent department of environmental protection discovers that data transmitted from the automatic monitoring equipment for water pollutant discharge of a key pollutant discharging unit is abnormal, it shall promptly conduct an investigation.

Article 25 The State shall establish a monitoring system for water environment quality and for water pollutant discharge. The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall be responsible for formulating water environment monitoring standards, uniformly releasing national water environment status information, organizing monitoring networks together with the competent department of water administration and other departments under the State Council, uniformly planning the distribution of national water environment quality monitoring stations (points), establishing a monitoring data sharing mechanism, and strengthening the management of water environment monitoring.

Article 26 The water resources protection institutions for the basins of important rivers and lakes determined by the State shall be responsible for monitoring the water environment quality conditions of the provincial boundary water bodies within their respective basins, and shall promptly report the monitoring results to the competent department of environmental protection under the State Council and the competent department of water administration under the State Council; where a leading body for basin water resources protection established with the approval of the State Council exists, the monitoring results shall be promptly reported to that leading body.

Article 27 When developing, utilizing, regulating, and dispatching water resources, the relevant departments under the State Council and local people's governments at or above the county level shall take all factors into consideration, maintain the reasonable flow of rivers and the reasonable water levels of lakes, reservoirs, and groundwater bodies, ensure basic ecological water use, and preserve the ecological functions of water bodies.

Article 28 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of water administration and other relevant departments under the State Council and the relevant people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, establish a joint coordination mechanism for water environmental protection in the basins of important rivers and lakes, and implement unified planning, unified standards, unified monitoring, and unified prevention and control measures.

Article 29 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council and the competent departments of environmental protection under the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, together with the relevant departments at the same level, based on the ecological and environmental function needs of the river basin, define the requirements for basin ecological environmental protection, organize and carry out monitoring and evaluation of the basin's environmental resource carrying capacity, and implement an early warning system for the basin's environmental resource carrying capacity.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, based on the ecological and environmental function needs of the river basin, organize and carry out the protection and restoration of rivers, lakes, and wetlands, construct ecological environment treatment and protection projects such as constructed wetlands, water conservation forests, vegetation buffer strips and isolation belts along rivers and lakes in light of local conditions, remediate black and odorous water bodies, and enhance the environmental resource carrying capacity of the river basin.
Any development and construction activities shall take effective measures to maintain the ecological and environmental functions of the river basin and strictly adhere to the ecological protection red line.

Article 30 The competent department of environmental protection and other departments that exercise supervision and management authority in accordance with this Law shall have the power to conduct on-site inspections of pollutant discharging units within their jurisdiction, and the units being inspected shall truthfully report the situation and provide necessary materials. The inspecting authorities shall have the obligation to keep confidential any trade secrets obtained during the inspection.

Article 31 Water pollution disputes across administrative regions shall be resolved through consultation between the relevant local people's governments, or through coordination by their common higher-level people's government.

Article 32 The competent department of environmental protection under the State Council shall, together with the competent department of health under the State Council, based on the degree of harm and impact on public health and the ecological environment, publish a list of toxic and harmful water pollutants and implement risk management.
Enterprises, institutions, and other producers and operators that discharge the toxic and harmful water pollutants listed in the list specified in the preceding paragraph shall monitor the discharge outlets and the surrounding environment, assess environmental risks, investigate and eliminate environmental safety hazards, disclose information on the toxic and harmful water pollutants, and take effective measures to prevent environmental risks.

Article 33 It is prohibited to discharge into water bodies any oil, acid, alkali, or highly toxic waste liquid.
It is prohibited to clean vehicles and containers that have been used for storing oil or toxic pollutants in water bodies.

Article 34 It is prohibited to discharge or dump into water bodies any radioactive solid waste or wastewater containing high-level or intermediate-level radioactive substances.
Wastewater containing low-level radioactive substances discharged into water bodies shall comply with the relevant provisions and standards of the State on radioactive pollution prevention and control.

Article 35 Where wastewater containing heat is discharged into water bodies, measures shall be taken to ensure that the water temperature of the water bodies meets the water environment quality standards.
Article 36 Sewage containing pathogens shall be disinfected before discharge; it may be discharged only after meeting the relevant national standards.

Article 37 It is prohibited to discharge or dump into water bodies any industrial solid waste, urban garbage, or other wastes.
It is prohibited to discharge or dump into water bodies or directly bury underground any soluble highly toxic waste residues containing mercury, cadmium, arsenic, chromium, lead, cyanide, yellow phosphorus, or the like.
For sites storing soluble highly toxic waste residues, measures shall be taken to prevent water ingress, seepage, and loss.
Article 38 It is prohibited to pile up or store solid waste and other pollutants on the beaches and banks below the highest water level lines of rivers, lakes, canals, ditches, and reservoirs.

Article 39 It is prohibited to discharge water pollutants through means that evade supervision and management, such as using seepage wells, seepage pits, fissures, karst caves, privately setting up concealed pipes, tampering with or falsifying monitoring data, or operating water pollution prevention and control facilities abnormally.

Article 40 Chemical production enterprises and the operation and management units of industrial agglomeration areas, mining areas, tailings ponds, hazardous waste disposal sites, landfill sites, etc., shall take measures such as anti-seepage and construct groundwater quality monitoring wells for monitoring to prevent groundwater pollution.
Underground oil tanks of gas stations and the like shall use double-layer tanks or adopt other effective measures such as building anti-seepage pools, and shall conduct anti-seepage monitoring to prevent groundwater pollution.
It is prohibited to use ditches, pits, or ponds without anti-seepage measures to convey or store wastewater containing toxic pollutants, sewage containing pathogens, or other wastes.

Article 41 Where the water quality of aquifers in multi-layer groundwater differs significantly, extraction shall be conducted by layer; the polluted phreatic water and confined water shall not be extracted together.

Article 42 When constructing underground engineering facilities or carrying out underground exploration, mining, or other activities, protective measures shall be taken to prevent groundwater pollution.
Abandoned mines, drilling wells, water intake wells, etc., shall be sealed or backfilled.
Article 43 Artificial recharge to replenish groundwater shall not deteriorate the quality of the groundwater.

Article 44 The relevant departments under the State Council and local people's governments at or above the county level shall rationally plan the industrial layout, require enterprises causing water pollution to carry out technological transformation, adopt comprehensive prevention and control measures, increase the reuse rate of water, and reduce the discharge amount of wastewater and pollutants.

Article 45 Enterprises discharging industrial wastewater shall take effective measures to collect and treat all the wastewater generated, so as to prevent environmental pollution. Industrial wastewater containing toxic and harmful water pollutants shall be collected and treated separately and shall not be discharged after dilution.
Industrial agglomeration areas shall be equipped with corresponding centralized sewage treatment facilities, install automatic monitoring equipment, connect with the monitoring equipment of the competent department of environmental protection, and ensure the normal operation of the monitoring equipment.
Where industrial wastewater is discharged into centralized sewage treatment facilities, it shall be pretreated in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, and may be discharged only after meeting the treatment process requirements of the centralized treatment facilities.

Article 46 The State shall implement a system for eliminating backward technologies and equipment that cause serious water pollution.
The department of comprehensive economic macro-control under the State Council, together with the relevant departments under the State Council, shall publish a list of technologies that cause serious water pollution and are prohibited to be used within a prescribed time limit, and a list of equipment that causes serious water pollution and are prohibited to be produced, sold, imported, or used within a prescribed time limit.
Producers, sellers, importers, or users shall stop producing, selling, importing, or using the equipment listed in the equipment list specified in the preceding paragraph within the prescribed time limit. Users of the technologies shall stop using the technologies listed in the technology list specified in the preceding paragraph within the prescribed time limit.
The equipment eliminated in accordance with paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article shall not be transferred to others for use.

Article 47 The State prohibits the construction of new small-scale production projects that do not conform to the national industrial policies, such as those for papermaking, leather tanning, printing and dyeing, dyestuff, coking, sulfur refining, arsenic refining, mercury refining, oil refining, electroplating, pesticides, asbestos, cement, glass, steel, thermal power, and other projects that seriously pollute the water environment.

Article 48 Enterprises shall adopt clean production processes with high raw material utilization efficiency and low pollutant discharge, and shall strengthen management to reduce the generation of water pollutants.

Article 49 Urban sewage shall be treated in a centralized manner.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall raise funds through financial budgets and other channels, make overall arrangements for the construction of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipeline networks, and increase the collection rate and treatment rate of urban sewage within their respective administrative regions.
The competent department of construction under the State Council shall, together with the departments of comprehensive economic macro-control and environmental protection under the State Council, organize the formulation of a national plan for the construction of urban sewage treatment facilities based on urban and rural plans and water pollution prevention and control plans. Local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize the departments of construction, comprehensive economic macro-control, environmental protection, and water administration to formulate plans for the construction of urban sewage treatment facilities within their respective administrative regions. The competent departments of construction under local people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the plans for the construction of urban sewage treatment facilities, organize the construction of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities and supporting pipeline networks, and strengthen the supervision and management of the operation of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities.
The operating units of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities shall, in accordance with the provisions of the State, provide paid sewage treatment services to sewage dischargers, collect sewage treatment fees, and ensure the normal operation of the centralized sewage treatment facilities. The collected sewage treatment fees shall be used for the construction, operation, and sludge treatment and disposal of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities and shall not be misappropriated for other purposes.
The specific measures for the collection, management, and use of sewage treatment fees for centralized urban sewage treatment facilities shall be prescribed by the State Council.

Article 50 The discharge of water pollutants into centralized urban sewage treatment facilities shall comply with the water pollutant discharge standards prescribed by the State or local authorities.
The operating units of centralized urban sewage treatment facilities shall be responsible for the quality of the effluent from such facilities.
The competent department of environmental protection shall supervise and inspect the quality and quantity of the effluent from centralized urban sewage treatment facilities.

Article 51 The operating unit of a centralized urban sewage treatment facility or the sludge treatment and disposal unit shall safely treat and dispose of sludge, ensure that the treated and disposed sludge complies with national standards, and record the whereabouts of the sludge, among others.

Article 52 The State supports the construction of rural sewage and garbage treatment facilities and promotes centralized treatment of rural sewage and garbage.
Local people's governments at all levels shall make overall plans for the construction of rural sewage and garbage treatment facilities and ensure their normal operation.
Article 53 The formulation of quality standards and use standards for products such as chemical fertilizers and pesticides shall meet the requirements of water environment protection.

Article 54 The use of pesticides shall comply with the relevant provisions and standards of the State on safe use of pesticides.
Transportation, storage of pesticides, and disposal of expired and invalid pesticides shall be strictly managed to prevent water pollution.

Article 55 The competent agricultural departments and other relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall take measures to guide agricultural producers in the scientific and rational application of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, promote soil testing and formulated fertilization technologies and highly effective, low-toxicity, and low-residue pesticides, and control the excessive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides to prevent water pollution.

Article 56 The State supports livestock and poultry farms and breeding communities in constructing facilities for comprehensive utilization or harmless treatment of livestock and poultry manure and wastewater.
Livestock and poultry farms and breeding communities shall ensure the normal operation of their facilities for comprehensive utilization or harmless treatment of livestock and poultry manure and wastewater, ensure up-to-standard discharge of sewage, and prevent water environment pollution.
The county and township people's governments of areas with dense free-range livestock and poultry breeding shall organize household collection, centralized treatment, and utilization of livestock and poultry manure and sewage.
Article 57 Aquaculture shall protect the ecological environment of waters, scientifically determine breeding density, and rationally use bait and drugs to prevent water environment pollution.

Article 58 Water for farmland irrigation shall meet the corresponding water quality standards to prevent pollution of soil, groundwater, and agricultural products.
Discharge of industrial wastewater or medical sewage into farmland irrigation channels is prohibited. Where urban sewage and livestock and poultry breeding wastewater not comprehensively utilized and agricultural product processing wastewater are discharged into farmland irrigation channels, the water quality at the nearest downstream irrigation water intake point shall be ensured to meet the farmland irrigation water quality standards.

Article 59 Discharge of oily sewage and domestic sewage from ships shall comply with the ship pollutant discharge standards. Ships engaged in ocean shipping entering inland rivers and ports shall comply with the inland river ship pollutant discharge standards.
Residual oil and waste oil from ships shall be recovered and are prohibited from being discharged into waters.
Dumping of ship garbage into waters is prohibited.
When loading and transporting oil or toxic cargo, ships shall take measures to prevent overflow and leakage and to prevent cargo from falling into water and causing water pollution.
International voyage ships entering the inland rivers of the People's Republic of China that discharge ballast water shall use ballast water treatment devices or take other equivalent measures to inactivate the ballast water. Discharge of ship ballast water that does not comply with regulations is prohibited.

Article 60 Ships shall be equipped with corresponding anti-pollution equipment and appliances in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and hold lawful and valid certificates and documents for preventing water environment pollution.
Ships performing operations involving pollutant discharge shall strictly abide by the operating procedures and truthfully record them in the corresponding logbooks.

Article 61 The municipal and county people's governments of the localities of ports, docks, loading and unloading stations, and ship repair yards shall make overall plans for the construction of facilities for the reception, transfer, and treatment and disposal of ship pollutants and wastes.
Ports, docks, loading and unloading stations, and ship repair yards shall have sufficient reception facilities for ship pollutants and wastes. Units engaged in the reception operation of ship pollutants and wastes, or engaged in the cleaning operation of ship tanks carrying oil or pollution-hazardous cargo, shall have reception and treatment capacity commensurate with their operation scale.

Article 62 Ships and relevant operating units engaging in operational activities with pollution risks shall take effective measures in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and standards to prevent water pollution. The maritime administrative agency and the competent fishery department shall strengthen supervision and management over ships and relevant operational activities.
For lightering operations of bulk liquid pollution-hazardous cargo, a ship shall prepare an operation plan, take effective safety and pollution prevention measures, and report to the maritime administrative agency at the place of operation for approval.
Ship dismantling operations by beaching are prohibited.

Article 63 The State establishes a drinking water source protection zone system. Drinking water source protection zones are divided into first-grade protection zones and second-grade protection zones; where necessary, a certain area may be delineated outside the drinking water source protection zone as a quasi-protection zone.
The delineation of drinking water source protection zones shall be proposed by the relevant municipal or county people's government and submitted to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval; for drinking water source protection zones spanning cities or counties, the relevant municipal and county people's governments shall negotiate to propose a delineation plan and submit it to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval; if negotiation fails, the competent environmental protection department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government shall, jointly with the water administrative, land and resources, health, and construction departments at the same level, propose a delineation plan, after soliciting opinions from relevant departments at the same level, and submit it to the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for approval.
For drinking water source protection zones spanning provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, the relevant people's governments of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government shall consult with the relevant river basin management agency to delineate them; if negotiation fails, the competent environmental protection department of the State Council shall, jointly with the water administrative, land and resources, health, and construction departments at the same level, propose a delineation plan, after soliciting opinions from relevant departments of the State Council, and submit it to the State Council for approval.
The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, according to the actual needs of protecting drinking water sources, adjust the scope of drinking water source protection zones to ensure the safety of drinking water. The relevant local people's government shall set up clear geographical landmarks and conspicuous warning signs at the boundaries of drinking water source protection zones.
Article 64 Setting up sewage outlets in drinking water source protection zones is prohibited.

Article 65 Construction, renovation, and expansion of construction projects unrelated to water supply facilities and water source protection are prohibited in first-grade drinking water source protection zones; existing construction projects unrelated to water supply facilities and water source protection shall be ordered to be demolished or closed by the people's government at or above the county level.
Cage culture, tourism, swimming, angling, or other activities that may pollute drinking water bodies are prohibited in first-grade drinking water source protection zones.

Article 66 Construction, renovation, and expansion of construction projects that discharge pollutants are prohibited in second-grade drinking water source protection zones; existing construction projects that discharge pollutants shall be ordered to be demolished or closed by the people's government at or above the county level.
Where cage culture, tourism, or other activities are engaged in within second-grade drinking water source protection zones, measures shall be taken in accordance with regulations to prevent pollution of drinking water bodies.

Article 67 Construction and expansion of construction projects that cause serious water pollution are prohibited in quasi-protection zones of drinking water sources; renovation of construction projects shall not increase the amount of pollutant discharge.

Article 68 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall, according to the actual needs of protecting drinking water sources, take engineering measures or build ecological protection measures such as wetlands and water conservation forests in quasi-protection zones to prevent water pollutants from being directly discharged into drinking water bodies and ensure the safety of drinking water.

Article 69 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize the environmental protection and other departments to investigate and assess the environmental conditions and pollution risks of drinking water source protection zones, recharge areas of groundwater-type drinking water sources, and areas surrounding water supply units, screen potential pollution risk factors, and take corresponding risk prevention measures.
Where a drinking water source is polluted and may threaten the safety of water supply, the competent environmental protection department shall order the relevant enterprises, public institutions, and other producers and business operators to take measures such as stopping the discharge of water pollutants, and shall notify the drinking water supply unit and the water supply, health, and water administrative departments; where it is cross-administrative region, it shall also notify the relevant local people's government.

Article 70 The people's government of a city supplied by a single water source shall construct an emergency water source or a backup water source; areas with conditions may carry out regional networked water supply.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall reasonably arrange and layout rural drinking water sources; areas with conditions may adopt methods such as extending urban water supply networks or constructing cross-village, cross-township contiguous centralized water supply projects to develop large-scale centralized water supply.

Article 71 Drinking water supply units shall perform water quality testing at the water intake and discharge outlets. Where the water quality at the intake does not meet the drinking water source water quality standards or the water quality at the discharge outlet does not meet the drinking water hygiene standards, the unit shall promptly take corresponding measures and report to the water supply competent department of the local municipal or county people's government. Upon receiving the report, the water supply competent department shall notify the environmental protection, health, and water administrative departments.
Drinking water supply units shall be responsible for the quality of supplied water, ensure the safe and reliable operation of water supply facilities, and guarantee that the quality of supplied water meets the relevant State standards.

Article 72 Local people's governments at or above the county level shall organize relevant departments to monitor and assess the drinking water safety status within their administrative regions, including the water quality of drinking water sources, water supplied by supply units, and water from user taps.
Relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall disclose drinking water safety status information to the public at least once per quarter.

Article 73 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government may, according to the needs of water environment protection, prescribe measures in drinking water source protection zones, such as prohibiting or restricting the use of phosphorus-containing detergents, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides, as well as restricting planting and breeding.

Article 74 People's governments at or above the county level may delineate protection zones for water bodies in scenic and historic areas, important fishery water bodies, and other water bodies of special economic and cultural value, and take measures to ensure that the water quality in the protection zones meets the water environment quality standards for the prescribed uses.

Article 75 No new sewage outlets may be constructed within the protection zones of water bodies in scenic and historic areas, important fishery water bodies, and other water bodies of special economic and cultural value. Where a new sewage outlet is constructed near a protection zone, it shall be ensured that the water body in the protection zone is not polluted.

Article 76 People's governments at all levels and their relevant departments, as well as enterprises and public institutions that may cause water pollution accidents, shall, in accordance with the provisions of the Emergency Response Law of the People's Republic of China, properly carry out emergency preparedness, emergency response, and post-accident recovery for sudden water pollution accidents.

Article 77 Enterprises and public institutions that may cause water pollution accidents shall formulate emergency plans for water pollution accidents, make emergency preparations, and conduct regular drills.
Enterprises and public institutions that produce or store hazardous chemicals shall take measures to prevent fire-fighting wastewater and waste liquids that may seriously pollute water bodies, generated during the handling of production safety accidents, from being directly discharged into water bodies.

Article 78 Where an accident or other emergency occurs in an enterprise or public institution that causes or may cause a water pollution accident, the unit shall immediately activate its emergency plan, take emergency measures such as isolation to prevent water pollutants from entering water bodies, and report to the local people's government at or above the county level or the competent environmental protection department at the place where the accident occurred. Upon receiving the report, the competent environmental protection department shall promptly report to the people's government at the same level and copy the report to relevant departments.
Where a fishery pollution accident is caused or a water pollution accident is caused by a fishing vessel, the matter shall be reported to the competent fishery department at the place where the accident occurred for investigation and handling. Where a water pollution accident is caused by other ships, the matter shall be reported to the maritime administrative agency at the place where the accident occurred for investigation and handling; if damage is caused to fisheries, the maritime administrative agency shall notify the competent fishery department to participate in the investigation and handling.

Article 79 Municipal and county people's governments shall organize the preparation of emergency plans for drinking water safety emergencies.
Drinking water supply units shall, based on the local emergency plan for drinking water safety emergencies, formulate corresponding emergency plans, submit them to the local municipal or county people's government for record, and conduct regular drills.
Where a water pollution accident occurs in a drinking water source, or another emergency occurs that may affect drinking water safety, the drinking water supply unit shall take emergency measures, report to the local municipal or county people's government, and make it known to the public. The relevant people's government shall, according to the circumstances, promptly activate the emergency plan and take effective measures to ensure the safety of water supply.

Article 80 Where the competent environmental protection department or any other department exercising supervision and management authority in accordance with the provisions of this Law fails to make an administrative license or handle approval documents according to law, fails to investigate after discovering an illegal act or receiving a report of an illegal act, or commits any other act of failing to perform duties in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 81 Where a party refuses or obstructs the supervision and inspection by the competent environmental protection department or any other department exercising supervision and management authority in accordance with this Law by means of delay, encirclement, detention of law enforcement personnel, or practices fraud during supervision and inspection, the competent environmental protection department of the people's government at or above the county level or the other department exercising supervision and management authority in accordance with this Law shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan.

Article 84 Where a sewage outlet is set up in a drinking water source protection zone, the local people's government at or above the county level shall order its removal within a time limit and impose a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if it is not removed within the time limit, it shall be forcibly removed, with the expenses borne by the violator, and a fine of not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 1,000,000 yuan shall be imposed, and the violator may be ordered to suspend production for remediation.
Except as provided in the preceding paragraph, where a sewage outlet is set up in violation of the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the competent environmental protection department of the State Council, the competent environmental protection department of the local people's government at or above the county level shall order its removal within a time limit and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan; if it is not removed within the time limit, it shall be forcibly removed, with the expenses borne by the violator, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the violator may be ordered to suspend production for remediation.
Where a new, renovated, or expanded sewage outlet is constructed in a river or lake without the consent of the water administrative department or the river basin management agency, the water administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level or the river basin management agency shall, within its functions and powers, take measures and impose penalties in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 86 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, equipment listed in the catalogue of equipment prohibited from production, sale, import, or use that seriously pollutes the water environment is produced, sold, imported, or used, or a process listed in the catalogue of processes prohibited from adoption that seriously pollutes the water environment is adopted, the comprehensive economic macro-control department of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the comprehensive economic macro-control department of the people's government at or above the county level shall submit its opinions and request the people's government at the same level to order business suspension or closure.

Article 87 Where, in violation of the provisions of this Law, a small-scale production project is constructed that does not comply with the national industrial policy, such as papermaking, tanning, printing and dyeing, dyestuff, coking, sulfur smelting, arsenic smelting, mercury smelting, oil refining, electroplating, pesticide, asbestos, cement, glass, steel, thermal power, or other production projects that seriously pollute the water environment, the local municipal or county people's government shall order closure.

Article 88 Where the operating unit of a centralized urban sewage treatment facility or the sludge treatment and disposal unit treats or disposes of sludge that does not comply with national standards, or fails to record the whereabouts of the sludge, the competent urban drainage department shall order the adoption of remedial measures within a time limit and give a warning; if serious consequences are caused, a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan shall be imposed; if remedial measures are not taken within the time limit, the competent urban drainage department may designate a unit with the capacity to carry out the remedial measures on behalf of the violator, with the expenses borne by the violator.

Article 89 Where a ship is not equipped with corresponding anti-pollution equipment and appliances, or does not hold lawful and valid certificates and documents for preventing water environment pollution, the maritime administrative agency or the competent fishery department shall, within their respective functions and duties, order correction within a time limit and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan; if correction is not made within the time limit, the ship shall be ordered to temporarily cease navigation.
Where a ship performing operations involving pollutant discharge fails to comply with the operating procedures or fails to truthfully record in the corresponding logbooks, the maritime administrative agency or the competent fishery department shall, within their respective functions and duties, order correction and impose a fine of not less than 2,000 yuan but not more than 20,000 yuan.

Article 92 Where the water quality of a drinking water supply unit does not meet the standards prescribed by the State, the competent water supply department of the local municipal or county people's government shall order correction and impose a fine of not less than 20,000 yuan but not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, the matter shall be submitted to the people's government with the authority to approve for approval to order business suspension for rectification; the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

Article 94 Where an enterprise or public institution, in violation of the provisions of this Law, causes a water pollution accident, in addition to bearing compensation liability according to law, the competent environmental protection department of the people's government at or above the county level shall impose a fine in accordance with the provisions of the second paragraph of this Article, and order the adoption of remedial measures within a time limit to eliminate pollution; if the remedial measures are not taken as required or the unit lacks the capacity to do so, the competent environmental protection department shall designate a unit with the capacity to carry out the remedial measures on behalf of the violator, with the expenses borne by the violator; if a major or extraordinarily serious water pollution accident is caused, the matter may also be submitted to the people's government with the authority to approve for approval to order closure; the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons may be imposed a fine of not more than 50% of their income from the unit in the previous year; if any of the acts of illegally discharging water pollutants as specified in Article 63 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China is committed and does not constitute a crime, the public security organ shall impose detention of not less than 10 days but not more than 15 days on the directly responsible person in charge and other directly responsible persons; if the circumstances are relatively minor, detention of not less than 5 days but not more than 10 days shall be imposed.
For a general or relatively large water pollution accident, the fine shall be calculated at 20% of the direct losses caused by the accident; for a major or extraordinarily serious water pollution accident, the fine shall be calculated at 30% of the direct losses caused by the accident.
Where a fishery pollution accident is caused or a water pollution accident is caused by a fishing vessel, the penalty shall be imposed by the competent fishery department; where a water pollution accident is caused by other ships, the penalty shall be imposed by the maritime administrative agency.

Article 95 Where an enterprise, public institution, or other producer or business operator illegally discharges water pollutants and has been subjected to a fine penalty and ordered to correct, the administrative organ that made the penalty decision according to law shall organize a follow-up inspection; if it is found that the violator continues to illegally discharge water pollutants or refuses or obstructs the follow-up inspection, a daily continuous penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 96 A party who suffers damage due to water pollution shall have the right to demand that the polluter eliminate the hazard and compensate for the losses.
Where damage is caused by force majeure, the polluter shall not bear compensation liability, unless otherwise provided by law.
Where the water pollution damage is caused intentionally by the victim, the polluter shall not bear compensation liability. Where the water pollution damage is caused by the gross negligence of the victim, the polluter's compensation liability may be reduced.
Where the water pollution damage is caused by a third party, the polluter, after bearing compensation liability, shall have the right to recourse against the third party.

Article 97 Disputes over liability for damage and the amount of compensation arising from water pollution may, upon the request of the parties, be mediated and handled by the competent environmental protection department or the maritime administrative agency or the competent fishery department within their respective functions and duties; if mediation fails, the parties may institute legal proceedings in the People's Court. The parties may also directly institute legal proceedings in the People's Court.

Article 98 In a lawsuit for damages arising from water pollution, the burden of adducing evidence shall be borne by the polluter to prove the statutory grounds for exemption and that there is no causal relationship between its act and the damage result.

Article 99 Where there are a large number of parties suffering damage due to water pollution, the parties may, in accordance with law, elect representatives to conduct joint litigation.
The competent environmental protection department and relevant social organizations may, in accordance with law, support the parties suffering damage due to water pollution to institute legal proceedings in the People's Court.
The State encourages legal service institutions and lawyers to provide legal aid to victims in water pollution damage litigation.

Article 100 For disputes over liability for damage and the amount of compensation arising from water pollution, the parties may entrust an environmental monitoring institution to provide monitoring data. The environmental monitoring institution shall accept the entrustment and truthfully provide relevant monitoring data.
Article 101: Anyone violating the provisions of this Law and constituting a crime shall be investigated for criminal liability according to law.

Article 102: For the purposes of this Law, the following terms have the meanings as specified below:
(1) "Water pollution" means the phenomenon where, due to the introduction of certain substances into a water body, its chemical, physical, biological or radioactive characteristics are changed, thereby affecting the effective use of water, endangering human health or damaging the ecological environment, and causing deterioration of water quality.
(2) "Water pollutant" means a substance discharged directly or indirectly into a water body that can cause water pollution.
(3) "Toxic pollutant" means a pollutant that, after being directly or indirectly taken into the body of an organism, may cause disease, abnormal behavior, genetic mutation, physiological dysfunction, physical deformation or death of the organism or its offspring.
(4) "Sludge" means the semi-solid or solid substance produced during the sewage treatment process.
(5) "Fishery water body" means the water body designated as spawning grounds, feeding grounds, wintering grounds, migration channels of fish and shrimp, and the water body for breeding grounds of fish, shrimp, shellfish and algae.
Article 103: This Law shall come into force as of June 1, 2008.
